sources.entry: Nimclip - Native, local-first clipboard history manager with search, tags, image support, and quick paste.

summary.one_liner: Nimclip is a free, open-source, local-first native macOS clipboard history manager that lives in the menu bar and is opened with ⌘⇧V.
summary.what_it_does: Nimclip records text, links, code, images and rich text copied on the Mac, keeping the source app name and icon. Items can be searched (body text, OCR text from images, source app, tags) and filtered by type, favorited, and tagged with colored labels. Users can paste or copy items as plain text, merge several text items in selected order, and multi-select to delete with a confirmation. History is capped by count and retention time, with favorites exempt from automatic cleanup. Optional on-device OCR using macOS Vision indexes new images for search, and direct paste uses Accessibility permission to simulate pasting into the previous app.
use_cases: recover previously copied text or images
search past copied snippets and screenshots
merge several copied snippets into one paste
keep clipboard data private on a local Mac
how_to_run: Clone the project and open Cliplet.xcodeproj in Xcode, or run: xcodebuild build -project Cliplet.xcodeproj -scheme Cliplet -configuration Debug CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
Run tests with: xcodebuild test -project Cliplet.xcodeproj -scheme Cliplet -configuration Debug CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
Build a distributable ad-hoc signed ZIP with: ./package.sh arm64 (or ./package.sh x86_64)
Alternatively, download Nimclip-macOS-arm64.zip or Nimclip-macOS-x86_64.zip from GitHub Releases, move Nimclip.app to Applications, and open it
notable: Global hotkey (default ⌘⇧V) that can be re-recorded in settings; Option-hover preview of items
Multi-item merge: combine several text clips in chosen order and copy or paste at once
On-device OCR of copied images so images can be found by the text in them, with a manual backfill for older images
Automatic update checks against GitHub Releases, which send no clipboard content
Dark and light appearance and instant switching between Simplified Chinese and English
caveats: Requires macOS 15.0 or later and Xcode 16 with Swift 6 to build from source
Direct paste needs macOS Accessibility permission; without it, items are only copied for manual paste
Self-built or non-notarized builds may trigger Gatekeeper prompts on first open
